commands-and-routines-are-different-kind.description: a command is a memo, a routine is a procedure — the second exists to be invoked, the first exists to be remembered
commands-and-routines-are-different-kind.read_when: deciding whether a procedure becomes a routine or a memo, or which one a reader reaches for

hard-won-constraints-belong-on-the-recor.description: a non-obvious constraint with a measurement behind it belongs in memos — the manual is the source, memos are the surface a cold agent lands on
hard-won-constraints-belong-on-the-recor.read_when: writing any rule into a config file, or deciding whether the rule needs a memo or just a code comment

the-record-is-what-persists-when-the-lay.description: the four registers that measured five branches and a `kind: type` for each, in this repo and the kern one, all collapsed to the same shape — memos
the-record-is-what-persists-when-the-lay.read_when: asking where a doc, an index or a gate should live

the-frontier-law.description: the tree is only what is current; git is the archive — no shims, no changelogs, no code without a caller
the-frontier-law.read_when: before adding a comment, a backup file, or a changelog

the-index-is-derived.description: the index is a fold over the memos, regenerated whole, never hand-edited — a hand index drifts the day a memo moves
the-index-is-derived.read_when: adding an index, or asking why memos/README-style tables are generated
